title: The preparation of a TCG guarantee claim on the target: no window value, no home for the default-conditions date, no checklist interface, no agent binding, no state map, no service event and no message for a missing scheme document
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-013); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md; _work/msr/context/S3.md
description: Seven values the preparation slice needs are fixed by no source: the value of the preparation window of R-GUA-04, since the rule states the condition as days to claim_deadline <= the window and no document gives the window, the only figure carried being the 5 working day service level of the same rule; the home of the date the default conditions are met, since R-GUA-01 starts the deadline from it and guarantee_claim has eight fields and none holds it, and no field identifier exists for it; the interface of the scheme checklist, since R-GUA-04 names the Workbench and the Document Hub as its systems and no operation, event or contract dependency exists for the document read; the runtime of the claim preparation agent of AC2, since no source binds FEAT-GUA-01 to the rwb-agent service and the Work Package records no dependency on it; the map between the seventeen rule states of the guarantee state machine and the five members of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS; the event set of the service, since the ownership rows give S3 no event type while the connection matrix shows rwb-reporting listening to S3; and the message for a missing scheme document or an unresolvable document reference, since the message catalogue read for this key holds no such identifier.
evidence: FSD S3 A2.1.3.1 gives R-GUA-04 as the claim preparation agent assembles the claim against the scheme checklist when days to claim_deadline <= the preparation window, and R-GUA-01 as start the claim deadline timer from the date the default conditions are met when guarantee_type = TCG scheme and scheme_code present, and states no value for the window and no field for the date. TSD S3 T3.1 lists DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 as id, case_id, claim_type, claim_deadline, claimed_amount, filed_at, paid_amount and status, so no column holds the default-conditions date, and T3.2 lists LOV-CLAIM-STATUS as PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID and REJECTED while T4 states 32 rules over 17 states with no map between the two vocabularies. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 gives R-GUA-04 a service level of 5 working days and names Workbench and Document Hub as its systems, with no interface. TSD S3 T5.2 reaches P5 for documents only through the published Java interface of the monolith, and the ownership rows of the context pack give S3 one table, two REST operations, no event and one workflow, GuaranteeClaimWorkflow. The legacy data table names recovery_case, timer, guarantee_claim, document, decision_log_entry and rule_row, so the timer table and the case fields are case-side artefacts.
area: Business rules, workflow ownership and document integration
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-guarantee service owner, the P7 rule owner and the P5 document owner
proposed: Confirm the preparation window as a rule-row parameter and the claim deadline as a workflow timer with a case timer raised from the stage report; publish the default-conditions date as a signal fact or as a field of the Logical Data Model; publish the scheme-checklist interface of rwb-document or bind the checklist to a client library; bind FEAT-GUA-01 to rwb-agent or confirm the unattended step; publish the map between the 17 rule states and LOV-CLAIM-STATUS; decide the service event set; add a message identifier for a missing scheme document.

title: The guarantee-claim resource contract: two contract stories on one resource, no read operation in the inventory, no checklist or document element and no retention rule
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-013); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (RWB-S3-E4013-CON and RWB-S3-E4014-CON); _work/msr/context/S3.md
description: Four values of the contract slice are fixed by no source or by two stories at once. First, the legacy family yields two contract stories, RWB-S3-E4013-CON and RWB-S3-E4014-CON, and both name the same two operations of TSD S3 T-A.1 on the same base, so one resource has two publishers unless the document is split by operation; this story freezes the base, the element naming rule, the required set, the template and the version and hands the update to the sibling. Second, TSD S3 T-A.1 lists two operations and no read, so no GET is published and the claim content of SCR-17 is whatever the create and update answers return beside the case read. Third, the scheme checklist and its documents have no field on guarantee_claim and no element identifier anywhere, so neither is a published element. Fourth, the retention and archive rule of a guarantee_claim row is stated in no source read for this key.
evidence: TSD S3 T-A.1 gives API-S3-001 POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims with right C and the Idempotency-Key header, and API-S3-002 PATCH /api/recovery/v1/guarantee-claims/{claimId} with right U and idempotency not applicable, with the error statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and no read operation; T-A.2 names GuaranteeClaimRequest, GuaranteeClaimUpdate and GuaranteeClaim. TSD S3 T3.1 gives eight fields and T3.0 the seven standard columns, and neither carries a checklist, a document or a retention attribute. FSD S3 A2.1.3.1 and A2.6.3.2 name the checklist and the document set as behaviour and give them no field. The split plan records the same legacy key twice, once as APP and once as CON, for RWB-E4-013 and again for RWB-E4-014, so the resource has two contract stories by construction. Neither TSD nor FSD states a retention or archive rule for a claim.
area: Contract ownership, API surface and data retention
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-guarantee contract owner and the platform API owner
proposed: Confirm the split by operation of the single guarantee-claim resource between RWB-S3-E4013-CON and RWB-S3-E4014-CON, or merge the two documents and keep one contract story per resource; confirm whether a read operation exists and add it to the inventory if the screen needs one; decide whether the checklist and its document references become fields of the Logical Data Model; state the retention and archive rule of a claim row.
